result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_k_regular()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is k-regular (all nodes have degree `k`). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14128-L14217){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_k_regular(k) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is k-regular](/assets/graphs/is-k-regular.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same six-node cycle on both sides, with badges showing every node has degree 2. Left: asking for k=2 matches every node, so is_k_regular(k=2) returns True. Right: asking for k=3 matches none of them (badges in the accent color), so is_k_regular(k=3) returns False even though the graph is regular." width="100%"} A graph is k-regular if every node has degree exactly `k`. For directed graphs, this means all nodes have in-degree `k` and out-degree `k`. This is `is_regular()` with the shared degree pinned to a specific value, which is useful when a particular structure is expected, for example: - checking that a ring is `2`-regular or a cubic (`3`-regular) design came out as intended - verifying the output of a random-regular-graph generator - confirming that every node has exactly `k` partners in a matching-style design (e.g. every participant reviews and is reviewed by `k` others) Degrees are computed from all edges: parallel edges each count, and in an undirected graph a self-loop adds `2` to its node's degree (in a directed graph it adds `1` to both the in-degree and out-degree). The whole graph is checked and the current selection is ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The required degree, a non-negative integer. In an undirected graph every node must have exactly `k` incident edge ends; in a directed graph every node must have both in-degree and out-degree equal to `k`. An empty graph is `k`-regular only for `k=0`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is k-regular, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} This is the stricter cousin of `is_regular()`: instead of asking "is every degree equal?", it pins down the exact value $k$. Empty graphs vacuously satisfy $k = 0$; cycles are $2$-regular; the complete graph $K_n$ is $(n - 1)$-regular; and paths are never regular because their endpoints have degree $1$ while interior nodes have degree $2$. On directed graphs the check tightens to both $\deg^-(v) = k$ and $\deg^+(v) = k$ for every $v$. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A cycle's nodes each have degree `2`, so it satisfies `k=2` but no other value of `k`: ::: {#ab382f82 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(6) graph.is_k_regular(2), graph.is_k_regular(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: ::: A complete graph `K_n` is `(n-1)`-regular, so it satisfies `k = n - 1` but not `k = n`: ::: {#bdbdd2a4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} n = 5 graph = ec.Graph().add_full_graph(n=n) graph.is_k_regular(n - 1), graph.is_k_regular(n) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: ::: Nodes with no edges at all have degree `0`, so an all-isolated graph is 0-regular but nothing else: ::: {#0ed5c843 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) graph.is_k_regular(0), graph.is_k_regular(1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: ::: In a directed graph both directions must match `k`. A directed cycle gives each node one incoming and one outgoing edge, so it is `1`-regular, not `2`-regular, even though each node touches two edges: ::: {#4d6224aa .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} directed_cycle = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_cycle_graph(n=4) directed_cycle.is_k_regular(1), directed_cycle.is_k_regular(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: :::
